description: Phase 4 — Tauri v2 mobile app for Android with keyboard management, extra keys integration, biometric auth, and mobile gesture refinements

userStories.title: Initialize Tauri Android target
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the Tauri project configured for Android builds so I can produce an APK.
acceptanceCriteria: CONTEXT7 RESEARCH: Use Context7 MCP tool to query Tauri v2 docs for 'android init setup configuration mobile prerequisites'. Use latest patterns found.
Set Android env vars in the build environment: JAVA_HOME, ANDROID_HOME, NDK_HOME
Run `cd ui && npx tauri android init` to generate the Android project in src-tauri/gen/android/
Verify the generated Android project structure exists
Run `cd ui && npx tauri android build --debug` to produce a debug APK
Document the APK location and size
If build fails, document the error and attempt to fix — common issues: NDK version mismatch, missing SDK platform, Gradle version
userStories.notes: IMPORTANT: Must set env vars before running tauri commands. Use: export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk && export ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/Android/Sdk && export NDK_HOME=$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/30.0.14904198 && export PATH=$PATH:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin. The Rust Android targets (aarch64-linux-android, etc.) are already installed. The `tauri android init` generates a Gradle-based Android project in src-tauri/gen/android/. The `tauri android build --debug` compiles both the Rust code (cross-compiled) and the Android wrapper.

userStories.title: Tauri keyboard plugin for mobile
userStories.description: As a mobile user, I want the app to properly detect keyboard show/hide events so the terminal and extra keys row resize correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: CONTEXT7 RESEARCH: Use Context7 MCP tool to query Tauri v2 docs for 'keyboard plugin mobile show hide height'. Use latest patterns found.
Research if tauri-plugin-keyboard exists for Tauri v2 — if not, document alternative approaches
If plugin exists: install it, add to Cargo.toml and tauri.conf.json, wire into platform/keyboard.ts
If no plugin: the web fallback (visualViewport heuristic from Phase 2) will be used on mobile too — verify it works in Android WebView
Update platform/keyboard.ts to prefer Tauri keyboard API when available, fall back to web heuristic
`cd ui && npm run check` passes
`cd ui && npm run build` passes
userStories.notes: Tauri v2 mobile keyboard handling may not have a dedicated plugin yet. The web fallback (visualViewport resize heuristic from Phase 2 platform/keyboard.ts) should work in Android's WebView. The key question is whether Tauri provides a native keyboard API or if we rely on the web fallback. Check @tauri-apps/plugin-* packages on npm and the Tauri plugins repository. If no native plugin, the web fallback is sufficient for Phase 4.

userStories.title: Biometric authentication plugin
userStories.description: As a mobile user, I want to unlock the app with fingerprint or face recognition instead of typing my password every time.
acceptanceCriteria: CONTEXT7 RESEARCH: Use Context7 MCP tool to query Tauri v2 docs for 'biometric authentication mobile plugin fingerprint'. Use latest patterns found.
Research available Tauri v2 biometric plugins (official or community)
If plugin exists: install and configure for Android
If no plugin: document the gap and create a placeholder in platform/biometrics.ts that returns 'not available'
Create `ui/src/lib/platform/biometrics.ts` with: checkBiometricAvailability(), authenticate() functions
Both functions return graceful 'not available' responses on web (no-op)
`cd ui && npm run check` passes
`cd ui && npm run build` passes
userStories.notes: Biometric auth on Tauri mobile is less mature than React Native. Check for: tauri-plugin-biometric, tauri-plugin-authenticator, or community plugins. If nothing exists, create the interface (biometrics.ts) with no-op implementations so Phase 5+ can fill in the native code later. The biometric flow: app launch -> check if enabled -> prompt fingerprint/face -> on success, retrieve session token from secure storage -> continue to app.

userStories.title: Mobile-specific Tauri configuration
userStories.description: As a mobile user, I want the Android app properly configured with correct permissions, screen orientation support, and status bar handling.
acceptanceCriteria: Configure Android permissions in tauri.conf.json or AndroidManifest: INTERNET (required for WebSocket/API)
Set app to support both portrait and landscape orientations
Configure the Android status bar to be transparent/immersive for maximum terminal space
Set minimum SDK version to API 24 (Android 7.0) in the Tauri Android config
Verify the app identifier matches: app.js-node.svrctlrs
`cd ui && npx tauri android build --debug` succeeds (with env vars set)
userStories.notes: The tauri.conf.json may need Android-specific sections. Check the generated AndroidManifest.xml in src-tauri/gen/android/ for permissions. INTERNET permission is usually auto-included. Screen orientation is configured in the activity tag. Status bar immersive mode can be set via Android theme in styles.xml or via Tauri window config. Set env vars before running: export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk && export ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/Android/Sdk && export NDK_HOME=$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/30.0.14904198

Verify Android debug APK builds: `cd ui && npx tauri android build --debug` (with env vars)
Document APK size, build time, and any known issues in progress.txt
Update CLAUDE.md with Android build commands and mobile notes
Push all changes
All quality checks pass
